header:
Date: 2026-04-25
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Omar Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Redwood CSM); Ethan Gomez, Sara Patel, Ravi Mehta (Lucent Media)
summary: Quarterly business review focused on usage trends (tokens/embeddings), cost drivers, recent reliability incidents, and alignment on roadmap (dedicated vs hosted, SSO/SOC2 requests). Agreed next steps include sharing detailed cost breakdown, running targeted benchmarks for production prompts, and scheduling a dedicated sizing deep-dive.
topics: Roadmap and feature asks (prefetching/KV cache tuning, lower-cost model variants)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining the QBR for Lucent Media. we've got about 45 minutes. quick roll call?
[00:08] Ethan Gomez: Ethan here.
[00:10] Sara Patel: Sara on the line.
[00:12] Ravi Mehta: Ravi here.
[00:14] Omar Ruiz: Omar from Redwood.
[00:16] Priya Patel: Priya CSM. thanks.
[00:20] Maya Chen: Great. agenda — usage/cost, reliability incidents, roadmap and security ask. Ethan do you want to kick off with how the team's seen usage?
[00:30] Ethan Gomez: Sure, yeah. So we've seen about a 28% q/q increase in token usage driven by a new personalization feature, embeddings for content search are up as well. cost has spiked in April, partly due to longer context windows and more retry traffic when we had that short outage on April tenth.
[00:50] Sara Patel: just to add, some of the spikes were from backfill jobs we ran accidentally; our batch job had a duplicate run which doubled calls for a few hours, so that inflates number.
[01:05] Maya Chen: ok that explains part of it. Omar, do you have the cost breakdown by model/route?
[01:12] Omar Ruiz: Yep, I pulled preliminary numbers. most of the cost is coming from the prod text-generation route using redwood-llama-70b-q4 at longer seq lengths; embeddings are a smaller proportion but growing. There's also a small portion attributed to retries — we saw about 3% retry rate around the incident window which added tail cost. I'll share the detailed table after the call.
[01:35] Ravi Mehta: is the retry traffic from the service returning 5xx or timeouts?
[01:40] Omar Ruiz: mostly transient timeouts during the failover when we were routing across regions. the platform did automatic fallback but the client retried aggressively.
[01:50] Sara Patel: we should definitely tune the client retry policy, we have exponential backoff but it wasn't long enough for that outage.
[01:58] Maya Chen: Good. next topic — the April 10th outage. Priya can you summarize customer impact?
[02:05] Priya Patel: from our support logs: about 12% of requests during a 6-minute window experienced elevated latency and some 502s. No PII was exposed. You raised a ticket and our incident team created a postmortem and we've shared it in the incident doc link in the chat.
[02:22] Ethan Gomez: the impact was mainly on user-facing generation, some internal pipelines timed out. question — is there an SLA credit process we can start for incidents like this?
[02:30] Maya Chen: for Hosted customers we have SLA terms; for Dedicated customers there are SLA-backed latency and uptime targets. Ethan, I know Lucent is currently on Hosted with committed usage but not on a dedicated contract yet — correct?
[02:44] Ravi Mehta: correct, hosted with a committed spend tier.
[02:47] Maya Chen: ok. we can review credits case-by-case; we'll also go through options to reduce blast radius: dedicated pools, regional failover tuning, and client-level retry backoff recommendations.
[03:00] Omar Ruiz: coupling that, we recommended enabling prefix KV caching and lighter quantized model variants for some non-critical routes — that reduces cost and p95. we can set up a bench for your top 20 prompts.
[03:14] Sara Patel: are there quality tradeoffs when moving to a quantized variant?
[03:17] Omar Ruiz: generally minimal for many prompt types; some long-context generation may see marginal differences. we can run A/Bs and include your eval prompts.
[03:26] Ethan Gomez: that'll be important — we cannot afford customer-visible regressions. can you include a human eval or automated metric?
[03:33] Omar Ruiz: yes, automated rouge/bertscore plus spot human checks.
[03:36] Maya Chen: switching to security/compliance items: Ravi you had questions about SOC 2 evidence and SSO.
[03:42] Ravi Mehta: yeah, security team wants SOC 2 Type II report and details on KMS integration. also SAML SSO — we need SCIM provisioning for users.
[03:52] Maya Chen: we already have SOC 2 Type II for the platform; I'll send the artifacts. KMS integration is supported — we have docs on Bring Your Own Key with AWS KMS and GCP CMEK. SCIM/SSO is supported, Omar can follow up on SCIM mappings for role-based access.
[04:08] Omar Ruiz: I'll send the SSO/SCIM mapping doc and a short how-to. We'll also include audit log retention options — default 90 days, enterprise add-on for longer retention.
[04:18] Sara Patel: what about data residency for EU? some of our clients need EU-only storage.
[04:23] Maya Chen: we have region pinning for hosted, and Private deployment options for on-prem/VPC if you need EU-only. We can discuss Dedicated capacity in eu-west-1 or Private if regulatory needs require it.
[04:36] Ethan Gomez: cost estimate for Dedicated?
[04:39] Maya Chen: depends on committed throughput. Omar, can you propose sizing?
[04:42] Omar Ruiz: yes — I'll prepare a sizing doc with GPU counts, expected throughput, p95 latency, and TCO comparing hosted vs dedicated. propose we schedule a deep-dive with Ravi next week.
[04:52] Ravi Mehta: week of May 4 works.
[04:55] Maya Chen: noted. next — reliability/observability asks. Ethan you asked for token-level cost by route and per-model latency percentiles?
[05:03] Ethan Gomez: yes, token-level cost for the last 90 days and per-route p50/p95/p99. also we want trace correlation to our request ids.
[05:10] Priya Patel: we can enable request-id passthrough; there's a console toggle plus an example middleware to forward headers.
[05:18] Sara Patel: and is there per-route throttling so we can cap non-critical background jobs?
[05:22] Omar Ruiz: yes, per-route rate limits and quotas are configurable; we can set a lower priority route and burst capacity for critical paths.
[05:30] Ethan Gomez: great. on the roadmap side, one feature we'd love is prefetching/prompt caching at the prefix level — to help with repeated user prompts. any plan for that?
[05:39] Omar Ruiz: we have an internal project called SmartCache that does prefix caching and KV prefetching; it's in beta with a few customers and can reduce tokens for repeated queries by up to 40% depending on patterns. We can put Lucent in the beta if you want.
[05:52] Ravi Mehta: we'd be interested but need to know isolation and security guarantees.
[05:56] Omar Ruiz: beta includes per-tenant isolation; keys and cache stored in the same region with encryption at rest. we'll share the beta security sheet.
[06:05] Maya Chen: ok. quick tangent — competitors. Ethan, any vendor evaluation ongoing?
[06:09] Ethan Gomez: we did a small eval of Anthropic for chat safety and OpenAI for latency. open to Redwood's help on cost/latency comparison.
[06:18] Maya Chen: we'll include a short benchmarking appendix comparing model variants and cost per million tokens.
[06:24] Sara Patel: back to billing — we saw an unexpected invoice line for backup storage. can someone explain?
[06:31] Priya Patel: that looks like ingestion artifact storage for embeddings snapshot. I'll pull the invoice line and send details to Ethan and Ravi.
[06:38] Ethan Gomez: thanks.
[06:40] Maya Chen: any other questions?
[06:42] Sara Patel: one more — there's occasional 429s during heavy batch runs. is that client-side too?
[06:47] Omar Ruiz: likely a combination of client burst plus configured per-route quotas; we can raise quota for a given time window or set a batch window. We'll add guidance to avoid back-to-back bursts.
[06:56] Maya Chen: ok we'll capture next steps. recap — Redwood to share detailed cost breakdown and benchmark plan, run targeted bench for top prompts, propose Dedicated sizing, share SOC2/KMS/SSO artifacts, and enable request-id passthrough.
[07:12] Ethan Gomez: that covers it, appreciate the help.
[07:15] Maya Chen: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the docs and schedule the sizing session. Bye.
[07:20] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: some speaker labels approximate, occasional filler and run-ons, some product names transcribed as redwood-llama-70b-q4 which may be shorthand for the internal variant.
file_notes: This is a QBR / health-check style call; includes AE+SE+CSM from Redwood. Action items and next steps captured in metadata. Transcript intentionally contains minor transcription artifacts and informal speech patterns.
